pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.
Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.
Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).
Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

alphabet.title: The Somali alphabet: 26 letters, no silent letters
alphabet.explain: Somali's Latin alphabet is famously honest: every letter is pronounced, no letter is silent, and the five vowels come in short and long pairs (a/aa, e/ee, i/ii, o/oo, u/uu) where the length changes the meaning.

counting.title: Counting in Somali: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Somali builds numbers from its blocks: 6-9 is shan (5) + the number below it, 10 is laba iyo toban, and 11-15 is that same ten + the number. Once you see the pattern you can count as far as you like.
rules: There are no silent letters — the word is exactly what it looks like.
Vowel length matters: hal (one) vs haal? the long vowel is real.
The deep throat q (qof) is written with q: qof (person).
